problems.title: Isothermal helium expansion
problems.scenario: A piston–cylinder undergoes an **expansion at constant temperature**. The fluid is **helium** (ideal gas, $M = 4\ \text{kg/kmol}$, $R = 2.07\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$). The temperature is **100 °C**, the initial pressure **30 bar**, and the final pressure **1 bar**.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the **specific expansion work** $w$, in kJ/kg.
parts.hint: For an isothermal ideal-gas process, $w = RT\ln(P_1/P_2)$. Use absolute temperature.
parts.solution:
Isothermal ideal gas, so $Pv = RT$ is constant and the boundary work integrates to a logarithm:

$$w = RT\ln\frac{P_1}{P_2} = 2.07 \times 373.15 \times \ln\frac{30}{1}$$

$$w = 772.4 \times 3.401 = 2627\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

(Temperature $T = 100 + 273.15 = 373.15$ K.)

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the **specific heat** $q$ that must be transferred for the process to stay isothermal, in kJ/kg. (Is it supplied or released?)
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find $w$ in (a), use $w = 2627$ kJ/kg.
parts.hint: For an isothermal ideal gas, internal energy doesn't change ($\Delta u = 0$). Apply the first law $q - w = \Delta u$.
parts.solution:
For an ideal gas at constant temperature, $u = u(T)$ is constant, so $\Delta u = 0$. The first law $q - w = \Delta u$ gives:

$$q = w = 2627\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

Since $q > 0$, the heat is **supplied to** the gas — energy must flow in to replace the work it does while staying at constant temperature.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the **specific entropy change** $\Delta s$ of the helium, in kJ/(kg·K).
parts.hint: For an isothermal process you can use $\Delta s = q/T$, or for an ideal gas directly $\Delta s = R\ln(P_1/P_2)$.
parts.solution:
Two equivalent routes. Isothermal heat addition:

$$\Delta s = \frac{q}{T} = \frac{2627}{373.15} = 7.04\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$$

Or the ideal-gas entropy relation at constant $T$ ($c_p\ln(T_2/T_1) = 0$):

$$\Delta s = -R\ln\frac{P_2}{P_1} = R\ln\frac{P_1}{P_2} = 2.07 \times 3.401 = 7.04\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$$

Entropy rises because the gas expands to a lower pressure.

problems.title: Mixing chamber with heat loss — exergy destruction
problems.scenario:
Water (200 kPa, 10 °C) enters a mixing chamber at **150 kg/min**, together with steam (200 kPa, 150 °C). The mixture leaves at 200 kPa, 70 °C. The chamber loses **190 kJ/min** of heat to the environment at **20 °C** ($T_0 = 293.15$ K).

Given properties:

| | h (kJ/kg) | s (kJ/(kg·K)) |
|---|---|---|
| Water | 42.022 | 0.1511 |
| Steam | 2769.1 | 7.2810 |
| Mixture | 293.07 | 0.9551 |

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the **mass flow rate of the steam** $\dot m_s$, in kg/min.
parts.hint: Combine the mass balance $\dot m_w + \dot m_s = \dot m_{mix}$ with the energy balance (remember the 190 kJ/min heat loss).
parts.solution:
Mass balance: $\dot m_{mix} = 150 + \dot m_s$. Energy balance (heat leaves, so it sits on the outlet side):

$$\dot m_w h_w + \dot m_s h_s = \dot m_{mix} h_{mix} + \dot Q_{loss}$$

$$150(42.022) + \dot m_s(2769.1) = (150 + \dot m_s)(293.07) + 190$$

$$6303 + 2769.1\,\dot m_s = 44150 + 293.07\,\dot m_s$$

$$2476.0\,\dot m_s = 37847 \quad\Rightarrow\quad \dot m_s = 15.3\ \text{kg/min}$$

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the **entropy generation rate** $\dot S_{gen}$ of the chamber, in kJ/(min·K).
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find $\dot m_s$, use 15.3 kg/min ($\dot m_{mix} = 165.3$ kg/min).
parts.hint: Entropy balance: $\dot S_{gen} = \sum \dot m_{out}s_{out} - \sum \dot m_{in}s_{in} - \dot Q/T_0$. The heat leaves, so $\dot Q = -190$ kJ/min at the boundary temperature $T_0$.
parts.solution:
Steady-flow entropy balance with heat rejected to the surroundings at $T_0$:

$$\dot S_{gen} = \dot m_{mix}s_{mix} - \dot m_w s_w - \dot m_s s_s + \frac{\dot Q_{loss}}{T_0}$$

$$= 165.3(0.9551) - 150(0.1511) - 15.3(7.2810) + \frac{190}{293.15}$$

$$= 157.87 - 22.67 - 111.30 + 0.648 = 24.57\ \text{kJ/(min·K)}$$

It is positive, as the second law demands for this irreversible mixing.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the **exergy destruction (exergy loss)** of the chamber, in kJ/min.
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find $\dot S_{gen}$, use 24.6 kJ/(min·K).
parts.hint: Gouy–Stodola: exergy destroyed $= T_0\,\dot S_{gen}$.
parts.solution:
Destroyed exergy is the entropy generation valued at the dead-state temperature (Gouy–Stodola):

$$\dot X_{dest} = T_0\,\dot S_{gen} = 293.15 \times 24.57 = 7200\ \text{kJ/min}$$

This is the rate at which the mixing irreversibly wastes work potential — even though energy is conserved, this much exergy is gone.

problems.title: Adiabatic steam turbine (ideal-gas model)
problems.scenario: In a stationary steam turbine, steam expands **adiabatically** from **500 °C, 10 bar** to a final pressure of **2 bar**. Treat the steam as an ideal gas with constant $c_p = 1.846\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$ and gas constant $R = 0.4615\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the **exit temperature** at an isentropic efficiency of **100%**, in K.
parts.hint: First get $k = c_p/(c_p - R)$, then use the isentropic relation $T_{2s} = T_1 (P_2/P_1)^{(k-1)/k}$.
parts.solution:
Specific-heat ratio: $k = \dfrac{c_p}{c_p - R} = \dfrac{1.846}{1.3845} = 1.333$, so $(k-1)/k = 0.25$.

Isentropic expansion from $T_1 = 773.15$ K:

$$T_{2s} = T_1\left(\frac{P_2}{P_1}\right)^{(k-1)/k} = 773.15\,(0.2)^{0.25} = 773.15 \times 0.6687 = 517\ \text{K}$$

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the **actual exit temperature** at an isentropic efficiency of **90%**, in K.
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find $T_{2s}$, use 517 K.
parts.hint: For an ideal gas with constant $c_p$, $\eta_T = (T_1 - T_2)/(T_1 - T_{2s})$. Solve for the actual $T_2$.
parts.solution:
Turbine isentropic efficiency in temperature form:

$$\eta_T = \frac{T_1 - T_2}{T_1 - T_{2s}} \quad\Rightarrow\quad T_2 = T_1 - \eta_T(T_1 - T_{2s})$$

$$T_2 = 773.15 - 0.90\,(773.15 - 517) = 773.15 - 0.90(256.1) = 543\ \text{K}$$

The real turbine extracts less work, so the gas leaves hotter than the isentropic 517 K.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the **irreversible entropy production** $s_{gen}$ at 90% efficiency, in kJ/(kg·K).
parts.hint: Adiabatic, so $s_{gen} = s_2 - s_1 = c_p\ln(T_2/T_1) - R\ln(P_2/P_1)$.
parts.solution:
For an adiabatic device the entropy generated equals the entropy rise of the steam:

$$s_{gen} = s_2 - s_1 = c_p\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} - R\ln\frac{P_2}{P_1}$$

$$= 1.846\ln\frac{543}{773.15} - 0.4615\ln\frac{2}{10}$$

$$= 1.846(-0.3539) - 0.4615(-1.6094) = -0.6533 + 0.7428 = 0.0895\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$$

Positive, confirming the real expansion is irreversible (the isentropic case would give exactly 0).

problems.title: Polytropic compression of air — full analysis
problems.scenario: **0.5 kg** of air is compressed in a closed piston–cylinder along a **polytropic** path $PV^{1.25} = \text{const}$ from $P_1 = 100\ \text{kPa}$, $T_1 = 300\ \text{K}$ to $P_2 = 800\ \text{kPa}$. Take $R = 0.287$, $c_v = 0.718$, $c_p = 1.005\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the **final temperature** $T_2$, in K.
parts.hint: Polytropic $T$–$P$ relation: $T_2 = T_1 (P_2/P_1)^{(n-1)/n}$ with $n = 1.25$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the **boundary work** $W_b$, in kJ (sign: negative = work on the gas).
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find $T_2$, use 454.7 K.
parts.hint: For an ideal gas, $W_b = mR(T_2 - T_1)/(1 - n)$.
parts.solution:
$$W_b = \frac{mR(T_2 - T_1)}{1 - n} = \frac{0.5 \times 0.287 \times (454.7 - 300)}{1 - 1.25}$$

$$= \frac{22.20}{-0.25} = -88.8\ \text{kJ}$$

Negative, as expected for a compression — work is done **on** the gas.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the **heat transfer** $Q$, in kJ (state the direction).
parts.hint: Closed-system first law: $Q = \Delta U + W_b$, with $\Delta U = m c_v (T_2 - T_1)$.
parts.solution:
$$\Delta U = m c_v (T_2 - T_1) = 0.5 \times 0.718 \times 154.7 = 55.5\ \text{kJ}$$

$$Q = \Delta U + W_b = 55.5 + (-88.8) = -33.3\ \text{kJ}$$

Negative → about 33 kJ of heat is **rejected** from the gas during the compression.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the **specific entropy change** $\Delta s$ of the air, in kJ/(kg·K).
parts.hint: $\Delta s = c_p\ln(T_2/T_1) - R\ln(P_2/P_1)$.
parts.solution:
$$\Delta s = c_p\ln\frac{T_2}{T_1} - R\ln\frac{P_2}{P_1} = 1.005\ln\frac{454.7}{300} - 0.287\ln 8$$

$$= 1.005(0.4159) - 0.287(2.0794) = 0.418 - 0.597 = -0.179\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$$

Entropy of the gas **decreases** — consistent with heat being removed during the compression.

problems.title: Carnot heat pump vs. resistance heating
problems.scenario: A reversible (Carnot) **heat pump** keeps a house at **22 °C** ($T_H = 295$ K) while the outside is at **2 °C** ($T_L = 275$ K). The house loses heat at **60 000 kJ/h**, and the heat pump runs continuously to replace it. Electricity costs **€0.11/kWh**.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the **coefficient of performance** $COP_{HP}$.
parts.hint: For a reversible heat pump, $COP_{HP} = T_H/(T_H - T_L)$, temperatures in K.
parts.solution:
$$COP_{HP} = \frac{T_H}{T_H - T_L} = \frac{295}{295 - 275} = \frac{295}{20} = 14.75$$

A small temperature lift gives a very high COP.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the **electric power input**, in kW.
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find the COP, use 14.75.
parts.hint: First convert the heat demand to kW: $60\,000\ \text{kJ/h} \div 3600$. Then $\dot W = \dot Q_H / COP_{HP}$.
parts.solution:
Heat demand: $\dot Q_H = 60\,000/3600 = 16.67$ kW. Then:

$$\dot W = \frac{\dot Q_H}{COP_{HP}} = \frac{16.67}{14.75} = 1.13\ \text{kW}$$

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the **daily electricity cost** of the heat pump, in €.
parts.hint: Daily energy = power × 24 h; then multiply by €0.11/kWh.
parts.solution: $$\text{Cost} = \dot W \times 24\ \text{h} \times 0.11 = 1.13 \times 24 \times 0.11 = €2.98\ \text{per day}$$

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the **daily cost if simple resistance heating** were used instead, in €.
parts.hint: Resistance heating must supply the full $\dot Q_H$ as electricity (COP = 1).
parts.solution:
Resistance heating converts electricity 1-to-1 into heat, so it must draw the whole 16.67 kW:

$$\text{Cost} = 16.67 \times 24 \times 0.11 = €44\ \text{per day}$$

The heat pump costs about **1/14.75** as much — the COP advantage in one number.

problems.title: Real air turbine — exergy destruction
problems.scenario: Air ($c_p = 1.005$, $R = 0.287\ \text{kJ/(kg·K)}$, $k = 1.4$) expands through an **adiabatic turbine** from **600 kPa, 800 K** to **100 kPa**, at $\dot m = 2.0\ \text{kg/s}$. The isentropic efficiency is **0.85** and the environment is at $T_0 = 300$ K.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Find the **isentropic exit temperature** $T_{2s}$, in K.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Find the **actual exit temperature** $T_2$, in K.
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find $T_{2s}$, use 479.4 K.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Find the **specific entropy generation** $s_{gen}$, in kJ/(kg·K).
parts.hint: Adiabatic → $s_{gen} = s_2 - s_1 = c_p\ln(T_2/T_1) - R\ln(P_2/P_1)$.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Find the **specific exergy destroyed** $x_{dest}$, in kJ/kg.
parts.fallbackNote: If you couldn't find $s_{gen}$, use 0.0956 kJ/(kg·K).
parts.hint: Gouy–Stodola: $x_{dest} = T_0\,s_{gen}$.
parts.solution:
$$x_{dest} = T_0\,s_{gen} = 300 \times 0.0956 = 28.7\ \text{kJ/kg}$$

That is the work potential lost to irreversibility in each kilogram of air — the real turbine's shortfall versus the ideal one, valued against the dead state.
